During a `relation-departed` hook, relation settings can still be read (with relation-get) and a relation can even still be set (with relation-set), by  explicitly providing the relation ID. All units will still be able to see all other units, and any unit can call the `relation-set` hook command to update their own published set of data on the relation. However, data updated by the departing unit will not be published to the remaining units. This is true even if there are no units on the other side of the relation to be notified of the change.

Task execution: Each target's agent picks its task up from its watcher, runs it, and reports the status and results; the user cancels with `juju cancel-task` (see the action's operations and cancelling an action). The same watch surfaces serve script runs; the machine task notifications are the machine agent's queue (see the action watchers).

HA nodes: One record per Dqlite node in the high-availability cluster: the node's Dqlite identity and bind address, each uniquely indexed. Each node's satellites record the agent version it reports, the API addresses it serves on for agents to re-orient as the cluster changes, and the node password. High availability does not make a second controller; it makes more controller nodes running the same controller's database and API.

A bundle is nothing but declaration material: you write one as a YAML file that states the applications, their configuration, their relations and their machines, and you deploy it with one of Juju's clients: deploying requires model write access; an overlay customises it at deploy time, applied the same way.

HA expansion: The nodes are the HA cluster's membership; adding a node brings another controller agent into the controller's Dqlite cluster. Juju 4.1 has no `juju enable-ha` command; the `EnableHA` call on the controller API adds and removes the nodes.

In Juju, a script refers to any script you execute on a compute resource provisioned by Juju: a charm action or an arbitrary command. The two halves share the same records and machinery: the targets are units and machines, and what Juju persists is the execution, an operation with one task per target (see the action in the data model).

Deploy: `juju deploy <bundle> --overlay` reads the bundle as a YAML multidoc, snapshots the model status, builds the change graph and sorts it topologically. The client then applies each change in order through the ordinary operations: charms to add, applications to deploy, machines to request, relations to join, units to add, endpoints to expose, options to set, offers to create or consume. Any error aborts the whole apply.

Rule: A stored resource is immutable. An upload or a revision update writes a new record, repoints the application's usage at it, and schedules a removal job for the displaced record (see the resource removal below); the prior record and its content stay until nothing references them. A failed store removes the blob it just wrote.
